title: Codex stream helper records TOOL witnesses from codex exec --json events
description:
Split from task-7cc959e9b42043ba8009cdd9813103e0 (architect-e4b7eee0, 2026-10-30). This is the first slice, and it is independent of the wrappers.

Objective. Both wrappers already pipe `codex exec --json` into `node scripts/prompt-cache.mjs codex-stream` (moe-agent.sh ~7875, moe-agent.ps1 ~7041). Make that helper append TOOL witnesses to the file named by MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE. Use the format the Claude stream parser writes: TOP-relative, one path per line. Apply the Claude parser's success-only rules. No wrapper sets that env until the follow-up wrapper slice, so landing behavior is unchanged by this task.

Deliverable:
1. Spike. Capture real `codex exec --json` JSONL from the installed codex-cli (0.166.x; record the version) in a scratch git repo:
- an apply_patch file change that succeeds, and one that fails;
- a Serena MCP editing call that succeeds and one that fails, plus one with no result if you can reproduce it.
Embed the captured lines, trimmed, in the new test as fixtures, with the version and capture date. Expected schema (codex-rs exec events): `item.completed` items of type 'file_change' (`changes[].path`, `changes[].kind`, `status` 'completed'|'failed') and 'mcp_tool_call' (`server`, `tool`, `arguments`, `result.content[]`, `error`, `status`). Confirm whether paths are absolute, and how an MCP isError result surfaces.
2. New scripts/prompt-cache-witness.mjs. It builds a writer from the env names the Claude parser reads (moe-agent.sh STREAM_JSON_PARSER ~8238): MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE, MOE_GIT_TOP, MOE_GIT_REL and MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT. Port the parser's rules exactly:
- to_top_rel: an absolute path only inside TOP (case-insensitive on win32/darwin; the Git-Bash /c/ form on win32); a relative path gets the MOE_GIT_REL prefix; any `..` is refused. A path outside the repo prints `  [WARN] tool write outside the repo not harvested: <raw>` and writes no line.
- SERENA_TOOLS and serena_changed:
  - safe_delete_symbol counts only on 'OK';
  - rename_symbol counts only on 'Successfully renamed', and only its relative_path;
  - replace_in_files counts only the files its applied 'Replaced N occurrence(s) in M file(s):' summary lists;
  - a `{"result": ...}` wrapper is unwrapped first.
  Serena relative paths are joined to MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT first.
- A file_change witnesses each change path only when its status is 'completed'. An MCP call witnesses only when its status is 'completed', there is no error and a result is present.
- Appending is best-effort error handling: an IO error never breaks the stream.
3. scripts/prompt-cache.mjs codex-stream feeds each parsed event to the writer, which is a no-op when MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE is unset. Stdout and usage receipts stay unchanged.
4. Ship it. Add the file to moe-vscode/scripts/bundle-assets.mjs agentScripts (JetBrains already globs prompt-cache*.mjs). Prove it ships with a scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs assertion: a bundle missing it makes prompt-cache.mjs fail at import on every codex seat (mem:gotcha-clean-snapshot-missing-prompt-cache-helper).

NOT in scope:
- Wrapper or harness changes (the wrapper slice that depends on this).
- Remedy text and docs (task-7cc959e9).
- Gemini, Grok or interactive harvest.

Verification: `node --test scripts/tests/prompt-cache-witness.test.mjs scripts/tests/prompt-cache.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs`.
definitionOfDone: scripts/tests/prompt-cache-witness.test.mjs embeds real `codex exec --json` lines captured from the installed codex-cli, with the version and date noted: a successful and a failed file change, and a successful and a failed Serena MCP editing call.

With MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE, MOE_GIT_TOP, MOE_GIT_REL and MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT set, `node scripts/prompt-cache.mjs codex-stream` appends TOP-relative lines, proven by node tests that spawn the helper. Each path of a completed file_change is appended, relative paths prefixed with MOE_GIT_REL. So are the paths of a successful Serena editing call, joined to MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT first.

These append nothing, proven by node tests: a failed file_change; a failed, errored or result-less MCP call; a non-editing tool; safe_delete_symbol without 'OK'; a replace_in_files dry run; and a path outside the repo, which prints the WARN line.
Without MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE, codex-stream stdout and usage receipts are byte-identical to before: the existing scripts/tests/prompt-cache.test.mjs passes unchanged.

prompt-cache-witness.mjs ships in the VS Code bundle (bundle-assets.mjs, plus a local-runner-bundle.test.mjs assertion), and `node --test scripts/tests/prompt-cache-witness.test.mjs scripts/tests/prompt-cache.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs` passes.

implementationPlan.description:
Create scripts/prompt-cache-witness.mjs. It ports STREAM_JSON_PARSER's harvest rules (scripts/moe-agent.sh ~8231-8395) to codex exec --json events. The header comment cites that block, and says codex has no Edit/Write, so a file_change item stands in for them.
- Export createWitnessWriter(env = process.env, platform = process.platform), the idiom of createUsageReceiptWriter in usage-receipt.mjs. It returns { event(evt) }, a no-op when MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE is unset or empty.
- Normalize exactly as the parser does. MOE_GIT_TOP and MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT have backslashes turned into '/' and a trailing '/' stripped. MOE_GIT_REL is used as given: git --show-prefix, so '' or 'sub/'. Matching is case-insensitive when platform is win32 or darwin.
- toTopRel is to_top_rel:
  - On win32, '/c/x' becomes 'C:/x'.
  - An absolute path counts only under TOP + '/', and keeps its own spelling after that prefix.
  - A relative path loses any leading './' and gets the MOE_GIT_REL prefix.
  - A blank path, and a relative path with a '..' segment, are refused.
  - One tightening, which the task text asks for: an absolute path whose remainder has a '..' segment is refused too. The Python checks '..' only in relative paths, and refusing more fails closed.
- resultText is result_text: the text parts of result.content (a string, or a [{type:'text'}] list) joined by newline and trimmed, with a JSON {result: <string>} envelope unwrapped.
- SERENA_TOOLS holds the parser's 12 names. Match them on item.tool whatever item.server says, as base_name ignores the server.
- serenaChanged follows serena_changed:
  - safe_delete_symbol counts only on text 'OK';
  - rename_symbol counts only its relative_path, on text starting 'Successfully renamed';
  - replace_in_files counts only the summary lines after a REPLACED_HEADER match, each matching REPLACED_FILE, stopping at the first that does not, with lines split on CRLF, LF or CR;
  - every other tool counts its relative_path.
  A relative Serena path is joined to the Serena root, when one is set, before toTopRel.
- event(evt) acts only on evt.type 'item.completed':
  - an item.type 'file_change' with status 'completed' yields every changes[].path, whatever its kind;
  - an item.type 'mcp_tool_call' yields serenaChanged only with status 'completed', error null or absent, result a non-null object and arguments a plain object. Codex reports MCP isError as status failed with a result present, so the status check is what rejects it;
  - nothing else yields.
- For each yielded raw string, skip non-strings and blanks. A null toTopRel prints '  [WARN] tool write outside the repo not harvested: ' + raw with console.log. Any other result is appended with appendFileSync(file, r + newline, 'utf8').
- Error handling: one try/catch around the event body, and one around each append. A malformed event or an IO error (a missing dir, EISDIR, EACCES) never throws into the stream loop, like the parser's `except Exception: pass`. No state carries between events.
P1-P5 go green now. The spawned rows stay red until step 3.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Parse codex events inside the wrappers (Python in sh, PowerShell in ps1). Rejected: that makes two twins to keep in parity, while the node helper already sits in both codex exec pipelines and one witness file serves both wrappers. 2) Witness on item.started. Rejected: it precedes the apply (status in_progress), so a later failure would leave a forged witness. 3) Gate MCP calls on item.server === 'serena'.
